title: Heet: Accelerating Elastic Training in Heterogeneous Deep Learning Clusters
problem: Existing elastic schedulers for heterogeneous GPU clusters overlook heterogeneity in computation and communication, resulting in poor scaling efficiency and significantly prolonged job completion times.
motivation: Heterogeneous clusters are prevalent in modern data centers, and inefficient elastic scheduling wastes computational resources and increases time-to-solution for deep learning training jobs.
method: Heet measures how different the machines in the cluster are—both in how fast they compute and in how fast data travels between them. Using these measurements, it makes smarter decisions about where to place each training job and which machines to add or remove when scaling. This strategy reduces the harm that mismatched fast and slow machines would otherwise cause to training speed and job completion time.
key_novelty: Heet is the first elastic training scheduler (one that dynamically adds/removes machines during training) to account for both how fast different machines compute and how fast they communicate with each other.
contributions: Heterogeneity-aware elastic scheduler for distributed deep learning training
Characterization and modeling of heterogeneity impact on scaling efficiency
Improved job completion times compared to heterogeneity-agnostic schedulers
